transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I've started doing things at work and school that just don't really make any sense. Like, I work as a bookkeeping clerk, and lately I've been taking all the receipts and lining them up all the way across the floor. We get a lot of receipts from this local deli, actually. They make these amazing turkey sandwiches on rye, with like, this spicy mustard. I used to go there every Tuesday, but they changed their hours so now I can't really make it on my lunch break anymore, which sucks. 

But anyway, I've also been tapping my calculator in sets of nine. Just... tapping the keys nine times. It's a Casio, one of the older ones with the really clicky buttons. I love that sound, it's really satisfying. And then sometimes I'll just go stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, just holding them up until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. Which is usually Susan, our office manager. She's always over there complaining about the toner running out. Toner is so expensive these days, I really don't know how the company affords it with the way she prints every single email out. But yeah, I guess I'm here because I'm doing weird stuff like that.
Do you feel less anxious or more comfortable after lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator?

I'm not really sure... I don't know if it makes me feel less anxious or anything. I haven't really noticed a feeling like that. It's just nine taps. Nine is a really solid number, though. Like, there are nine innings in a baseball game. I used to play baseball back in high school, actually. I played shortstop mostly. Our coach, Mr. Henderson, he used to chew those big wads of Big League Chew bubblegum, the grape flavor. You could smell it from like all the way across the field. He drove this really loud, beat-up Ford pickup truck that he was always trying to fix himself, but it always sounded like the muffler was dragging on the ground. I think he spent more money on parts for that thing than it was even worth. But yeah, I don't really feel any different after I do the tapping or the receipts. I just kind of do it.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that others can't?

Well, yeah, sometimes. Like, if I'm just sitting alone at my desk, or when I'm walking home from my night classes... I'll hear this guy's voice. It's really clear, too. He'll say stuff like, "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I actually stop and look around, but there's never anyone there. 

It's kind of like that one street corner on my walk home, the one by the old hardware store? They have this huge neon sign that's supposed to say "Hardware," but the 'H' and the 'd' have been burnt out for like three months now. So it just says "ar ware," which sounds like some kind of pirate clothing brand or something. I actually went in there once to buy a hammer because my roommate broke mine trying to open a coconut. Can you believe that? A coconut. He bought it at this weird little fruit stand that popped up near our apartment. The guy running the stand was wearing this huge straw hat and kept trying to sell us these spiky fruits that smelled terrible. I think they were called durians? Anyway, my roommate swung the hammer, missed the coconut entirely, and cracked our kitchen tile. The landlord was so mad. But yeah, the voice... I hear it when nobody's around.
Do you think the lining up of receipts or the tapping of your calculator is in any way related to trying to calm yourself or make yourself feel better?

I mean, I don't really think it's about calming down. It's just... I just do it. Like I said, nine is just a good number. But speaking of feeling better, I actually tried this new herbal tea my mom sent me in the mail. She lives in Arizona now, and she's gotten super into all these desert plants and holistic stuff. She sent me this box of sage and chamomile blend, and the box had this really pretty painting of a mesa on it. I used to paint a little bit in high school, mostly watercolors. It's really hard to get the water-to-paint ratio right, though. If you use too much water, the paper gets all warped and wavy. I tried to flatten one out once by putting it under a stack of my heavy accounting textbooks, but it just made the pages of the books all wrinkly instead. My professor was not happy when I brought that book to class. He was this really strict guy who always wore bow ties. Every single day, a different bow tie. I think he had one with little calculators on it, actually. But yeah, I don't think the receipts or the tapping have anything to do with calming myself down.
Do you feel like you have to line up the receipts or tap your calculator, like something would be wrong if you didn't?

I don't think so. It's not like I feel like something bad is gonna happen or anything would be wrong if I didn't do it. I just... don't really have that feeling. But speaking of things going wrong with receipts, our main receipt printer at work completely jammed up on Tuesday. It just started spitting out this massive, endless roll of blank paper all over the floor. 

My coworker, Dave, he tried to fix it himself. Dave's always doing that, he thinks he's like this master technician just because he watches a bunch of DIY videos on YouTube. He actually tried to rebuild the transmission on his Honda Civic a couple months ago and ended up leaving the whole car sitting on cinder blocks in his driveway for like six weeks. His homeowners association got so mad they started fining him every single day. I guess the HOA where he lives is crazy strict, like they literally walk around with rulers to measure how tall your grass is. I could never live in a neighborhood like that. I like my apartment complex, even if the landlord is still annoyed about that cracked tile from the coconut. But yeah, no, I don't feel like I have to tap the calculator or anything like that.
Do you feel like you're in control when you're lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator?

I mean, yeah, I guess I'm physically in control. It's just... I actually came in because I've started doing these things at work and school that just don't make any sense. Like lining the receipts all the way across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or even just standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I'm okay. 

Usually it's Brenda who asks. She sits right near the copy room. She makes these incredible brownies for our office potlucks, actually. She puts walnuts in them, which I didn't think I'd like, because normally nuts in desserts are a total texture nightmare, you know? It's like when people put raisins in oatmeal cookies but they look exactly like chocolate chips, so you take a bite expecting chocolate and get a squishy grape instead. That is literally the ultimate betrayal. I bought a cookie like that from the vending machine in the student lounge at my night classes once, and I was so mad I almost threw it away. But I was starving because I had skipped breakfast. I usually just have cereal anyway, like Cinnamon Toast Crunch. The generic brand though, because it's way cheaper and honestly tastes exactly the same. But yeah, I am the one doing the things, I just don't really know why I do them.
Do you ever feel like you're thinking about something over and over that you can't stop thinking about?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I get stuck on thoughts like that. I mean, sometimes I'll have a song stuck in my head, like yesterday I had that jingle from the local mattress commercial playing on a loop. You know the one with the little cartoon sheep? I actually need a new mattress, honestly, because mine has this huge dip right in the middle of it. I tried rotating it last month, but it didn't really help at all. 

I was looking online at those ones that come vacuum-sealed and rolled up in a cardboard box, which is just crazy to me. How do they even compress a whole bed into a box like that? It feels like it completely defies physics. I took a physics class in high school and I was terrible at it. Mr. Henderson was the teacher, and he was always dropping random objects off his desk to prove gravity, like we didn't already know things fall down when you let go of them. He dropped a bowling ball once and it put this massive dent in the linoleum floor. The janitor, Gary, was so mad. Gary used to let me eat lunch in the boiler room when the cafeteria was too loud. But, uh, yeah, no, my thoughts don't really get stuck or anything.
Do you feel an internal pressure to perform these actions, like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator?

Internal pressure? Um, no, not really. I don't feel like a pressure building up inside me or anything like that. It's not like I'm bursting to do it. 

Speaking of pressure, though, the tire pressure light on my dashboard actually came on this morning on my way to work. It's that little orange horseshoe-looking thing with the exclamation point in the middle? I always panic for a second when it pops up, but it usually just happens when the temperature drops suddenly. The weather has been completely all over the place this week anyway. Like, Tuesday I was wearing a t-shirt, and then today I literally had to scrape frost off my windshield. I couldn't even find my actual ice scraper in the trunk, so I had to use an old gift card from my wallet. It was a gift card to Olive Garden that my aunt got me for my birthday last year. I still had like twelve bucks on it, which is kind of annoying because now the magnetic strip is totally ruined from scraping the ice. I love their breadsticks, too. They just keep bringing them out in those little baskets, which is amazing, but then you end up way too full before the actual pasta even gets to the table. I always get the chicken alfredo. But yeah, no, I don't feel any weird internal pressure to do the receipt or calculator stuff.
Do you feel like the receipts need to be lined up in a specific way or that there's a right and wrong way to do it?

A specific way? Um, no, I don't really think so. There isn't like a right or wrong way to it, I just sort of put them down wherever. 

But man, the thermal receipt paper they use at work gives the absolute worst paper cuts. I got one right on the webbing between my thumb and my pointer finger the other day, and it stung so bad every single time I used the hand sanitizer. They actually just switched the sanitizer in the dispensers by the elevators to this new brand that smells exactly like cheap tequila. It instantly reminded me of my 21st birthday last year. My friends took me to that Mexican place downtown, you know the one with the giant neon sombrero on the roof? Half the neon tubes were burnt out so it just looked like a glowing UFO from the highway. Anyway, my buddy Dave ordered these massive margaritas that came in glasses the size of birdbaths. I don't even really like tequila, honestly, I'm way more of a beer guy. Usually just whatever's cheapest on tap, like a basic lager or something. But yeah, no, there's no special order or right way I have to put the receipts down.
Do the voices you hear ever tell you to do specific things, like lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator?

Um, they don't really tell me to line things up or tap the calculator, no. But sometimes, like when I'm just sitting alone at my desk, or if I'm walking home from class, I'll hear this man's voice out of nowhere. He'll say things like, "check line seven," or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I always physically look around because I swear someone is standing right behind me. 

Speaking of walking home, though, they just completely tore up the sidewalk on 4th Street for some kind of water main project, so I've had to take this massive detour through the park lately. It's actually a nice park, but the squirrels there are getting ridiculously bold. One literally ran right over my shoe yesterday. I'm pretty sure people just feed them too much bread, which you aren't even supposed to do. Bread is actually terrible for wildlife, it like, expands in their stomachs or something. My mom used to take me to the pond to feed the ducks when I was a kid, but she always made us bring frozen peas instead. She'd buy those giant bags of generic brand peas from Costco. Costco is crazy on the weekends, honestly. I went there last Saturday just to get paper towels and there was a line backed up all the way into the tire center just for the free samples of pizza rolls. I didn't even get one because the lady ran out right when I got to the front of the table. But yeah, the voice just says stuff about line seven and signs, not really about the receipts.
Do you feel like the receipts or other things you line up need to be symmetrical or perfectly ordered?

Symmetrical? No, not really. I don't care if they're perfectly straight or anything. I just put them down. 

Speaking of straight lines, though, the lines they painted in the parking lot at my apartment complex are completely crooked. Like, whoever did it must have been half asleep or something, because if you park inside the lines on the left side, your right tire is practically in the next spot. It causes so many arguments. My neighbor in 2B—this guy named Gary—actually left a super passive-aggressive sticky note on my windshield about it last week. It was one of those neon pink Post-its. I use those exact same ones at work all the time to flag invoices that are missing signatures. Actually, our whole office supply order was messed up this month. We ordered blue pens, but they sent us these weird purple ones that look black until you hold them up to the light. It makes doing the ledger kind of annoying, honestly, because my boss hates purple ink. He says it looks unprofessional. He's super old-school like that, still wears a full suit and tie every single day even though it's just the four of us in the back office. But yeah, no, I don't really care if the receipts are symmetrical or anything like that.
Do you feel like lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator helps you feel more in control of your surroundings?

In control? Um, no, not really. Honestly, that's kind of the whole reason I came in to see someone. I've just started doing things at work and school lately that literally do not make any sense at all. Like taking the receipts and lining them all the way across the floor, or tapping the calculator exactly in sets of nine. Or sometimes I'll just end up standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. 

Which is super embarrassing, especially at the copier, because our machine is right next to the breakroom door. People are constantly walking past it to get coffee. We have one of those Keurig machines in there, but nobody ever empties the little pod tray when it gets full, so it just jams up. I tried to empty it last Tuesday and the old, wet coffee grounds spilled all over my sneakers. They were my good ones, too, the white high-tops I just got. I tried using one of those bleach pen things on the fabric, but it just turned the canvas this weird, gross yellowish color. I guess you aren't supposed to use bleach on certain materials. My aunt used to work at a dry cleaner downtown and she always told me club soda is way better for stains anyway. She actually met my uncle at that dry cleaner because he kept bringing in the same mustard-stained ties. But anyway, yeah... no, doing all that stuff doesn't really make me feel in control. It just doesn't make any sense to me.
Do you feel like something is forcing you to think about lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator?

Um, forced? No, I don't think anything is forcing me to think about it. It just sort of happens. I don't even realize I'm thinking about it until I'm already doing it, you know? 

Speaking of thinking about things, I've been trying to remember the name of this movie I watched last week, and it's been driving me crazy. It had that guy in it, the one who always plays the funny best friend, but this was like a serious role. They were on a submarine, I think? Or maybe a spaceship. It's so weird how those two settings look exactly the same in movies. Lots of grey panels and blinking lights. I actually wanted to be an astronaut when I was little. I even had this glow-in-the-dark star map on my ceiling. My dad spent like three hours putting all the little stickers up so they matched the actual constellations. But then the adhesive got old and they started peeling off one by one. I'd wake up and find a piece of Orion stuck to my pillow. It was a real pain to vacuum up, too. Our vacuum cleaner is practically ancient anyway, it makes this horrible screeching noise if you push it too fast on the carpet. But yeah, no, nothing is forcing me to think about the receipts or the calculator.
Do you feel like the things you do, like lining up receipts or tapping your calculator, have to be done in a very precise way?

Precise? I mean, I guess the calculator tapping is always in sets of nine, but other than that... no, not really. I just do it. 

Nine is a weird number, though, isn't it? Like how if you multiply anything by nine, the digits always add up to nine. My high school math teacher, Mr. Harrison, showed us that trick. He was a trip. He used to wear these really loud Hawaiian shirts every single Friday, even in the middle of winter. We lived up north, so it would be like ten degrees outside and he's standing there in short sleeves with palm trees all over him. He said it helped him pretend he was on vacation. I've never actually been to Hawaii, but I did go to Florida once for spring break. We drove the whole way down in my buddy's old Honda Civic. The AC was broken, so we had to roll the windows down, and the wind noise was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio. We ended up just yelling songs at each other for like fourteen hours straight. My throat was so sore by the time we hit Jacksonville I could barely talk for two days. But yeah, no, I don't think it has to be super precise or anything. It's just... I don't know, just something I end up doing.
Do you feel like you're doing these things because you're trying to get rid of a thought or idea that's stuck in your head?

Stuck in my head? Um, no, I don't think so. I'm not trying to push away any specific thoughts or anything like that. 

Speaking of things being stuck, though, the other day I got this massive wad of gum stuck right to the bottom of my shoe. Not the white high-tops, thankfully, but my black work shoes. I was just walking into the office, and I stepped right in it on the sidewalk. It's so annoying when people just spit their gum out wherever they want. I tried scraping it off on the curb, but it just smeared everywhere and made it worse. I ended up having to use a paperclip from my desk to dig it out of the little rubber treads for like twenty minutes. 

We have these giant boxes of paperclips in the supply closet at work, but they're all those plastic-coated ones in neon colors. I don't know who orders the supplies, but it looks so unprofessional when I have to clip a stack of audits or invoices together with a hot pink paperclip. My supervisor, Linda, she actually snapped at me once for using the green ones on a quarterly tax document. She's super particular about office supplies. She even labels her own stapler with this sparkly label maker. But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the thoughts. No, I don't have any thoughts stuck in my head that I'm trying to get rid of.
Do you feel like lining up the receipts or tapping your calculator is related to making things feel more orderly or balanced for you?

Orderly? Balanced? Um... no, not really. I don't think it's about making things neat or anything like that. I mean, my desk at work is a complete disaster zone right now anyway. 

Speaking of my desk, I spilled coffee all over my keyboard yesterday morning. Just a total mess. It was that cheap stuff from the breakroom, too, the kind that always tastes a little bit burnt no matter how much creamer you put in it. I had to run to the bathroom to grab a huge wad of paper towels, and of course, the dispenser jammed. It always jams if you pull too fast. The maintenance guy, Carl, he's always complaining about having to fix it. He carries this massive ring of keys on his belt, it jingles every time he walks down the hall. It sounds like a reindeer is coming or something. 

Actually, my mom used to collect these little ceramic reindeer figures. She had like twenty of them, all different sizes, and she'd set them up on the mantel every Christmas. One year, my cat—we had this fat orange tabby named Garfield, super original, I know—he jumped up there and knocked half of them off. It sounded like glass exploding. My mom was so mad, she wouldn't let the cat in the living room for a month. But um... yeah, no, the receipts and the calculator... it's not about making things orderly or balanced or anything. It's just something I do.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, have to be symmetrical or exact in any way?

Symmetrical? No, I don't... I don't really care if they're perfectly exact or whatever. I mean, they're just receipts. 

Though, you know, speaking of receipts, the thermal paper they use for them is actually super bad for you. I read this article the other day that said it's covered in BPA, like the stuff they put in plastic bottles that messes with your hormones. You're not even supposed to touch them if your hands are wet or if you just put on lotion, because it absorbs right into your skin. And I handle them all day at work. I started keeping a bottle of hand sanitizer on my desk, but it's that cheap generic brand that smells like cheap tequila. Every time I use it, I feel like I'm back at this awful frat party I went to my senior year of high school. My buddy dragged me to this college campus a few towns over, and the basement was just... it was completely flooded with spilled beer and whatever else. My shoes stuck to the floor with every step. I ended up throwing away those sneakers the next day. They were these really nice gray Vans, too. I had saved up for like a month working at the movie theater to buy them. Working there was actually pretty cool because I got to eat as much popcorn as I wanted, but the smell of fake butter gets permanently trapped in your hair. But um, yeah, the receipts don't have to be symmetrical or exact. I just line them up.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, have to be done in a specific pattern or arrangement?

A specific pattern? Um, well, I guess I do tap the calculator in sets of nine. And I don't just line the receipts up on my desk, I line them all the way across the floor. Honestly, that's kind of why I came in, because I've started doing all these things at work and school that just... they don't make any sense at all. Like the other day, I was just standing by the office copier with my hands held up in the air, just standing there until someone finally walked by and asked if I was okay. 

Speaking of the copier, though, it is literally always out of toner. And management refuses to buy the name-brand cartridges, so they get these cheap generic ones where the black powder just leaks everywhere. I got it all over my favorite shirt last week. It was this really cool vintage band tee I found at a thrift store downtown. I love thrifting because you can find the craziest stuff if you actually look. Like, once I found a fully functional waffle iron for three dollars. I made waffles for dinner for a straight week until I ran out of syrup. Have you ever tried that real, 100% maple syrup? Not the fake corn syrup stuff in the plastic bottle, but the real stuff in the glass jug from Vermont or wherever. It's so expensive, but it's totally worth it. My aunt lives up near the East Coast and she brings a jug down every Thanksgiving. Thanksgiving is usually a complete disaster at my house, though, because my uncle always insists on deep-frying the turkey and he almost burned the garage down two years ago. The fire department actually had to come out, and... wait. What did you ask me? 

Oh, right, patterns. Yeah, um, it's just stuff that doesn't make sense, like the receipts across the floor and the tapping in nines.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, are driven by a need to make things symmetrical or exact?

Symmetrical or exact? No, I don't... I think you asked me that already, actually. I don't really care about symmetry. They're just receipts. 

Though, honestly, I'm getting kind of sick of looking at receipts. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, so I just stare at numbers all day long. It's so boring. I only took the job because I needed something right out of high school, and my buddy's dad owns the firm. His dad is this super intense guy who always wears these really loud, striped ties. Like, neon green and purple stripes. It's blinding. He says it's his "power move" to distract people during negotiations, but I think he just has terrible taste. Actually, my grandpa had terrible taste in ties, too. He had this whole collection of novelty ties that played music when you pressed a little button on the back. He had one that played "Jingle Bells" and another one that played the "Macarena." He wore the "Macarena" one to my cousin's wedding, and it went off right in the middle of the vows. My aunt was furious. She didn't speak to him for like three months after that. But my grandpa just thought it was hilarious. He was always doing stuff like that, just trying to get a rise out of people. He used to hide fake plastic spiders in my mom's coffee mug. 

But um, yeah, no, the receipts don't have to be symmetrical or exact or anything. I don't really care about that.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, are driven by a need to make things perfect or just right?

Perfect or just right? Um, no, not really. I mean, they're just pieces of paper, so who cares if they're perfect? 

I definitely don't have time to make things perfect at work anyway. My desk is right next to the breakroom, and the microwave in there is always going off. People are constantly heating up the weirdest smelling lunches. Like, yesterday, someone microwaved leftover fish. Who microwaves fish in an office? It smelled like a pier at low tide for the rest of the afternoon. It reminded me of this time my family went to the beach when I was like ten, and my little brother found this dead jellyfish washed up on the sand. He poked it with a stick and then chased me down the beach with it. I ran so fast I tripped over a sandcastle some kid had spent all morning building. The kid started bawling, and his dad looked like he wanted to murder me. We had to pack up and leave early because it was just too awkward. We ended up stopping at this diner on the way home, and I ordered a chocolate milkshake, but the machine was broken, so they gave me strawberry instead. I hate strawberry flavor, it always tastes so artificial. Like that pink medicine they give you when you're a kid with an ear infection. I had so many ear infections growing up, I practically lived at the pediatrician's office. 

But, uh, anyway... no, I don't need things to be perfect or just right. I just do the receipt thing, I guess.

patient.answer:
Hi. Well, I came in because I've started doing things at work and school that just don't really make any sense. Like, I work as a bookkeeping clerk, and lately I've been taking all the receipts and lining them up all the way across the floor. We get a lot of receipts from this local deli, actually. They make these amazing turkey sandwiches on rye, with like, this spicy mustard. I used to go there every Tuesday, but they changed their hours so now I can't really make it on my lunch break anymore, which sucks. 

But anyway, I've also been tapping my calculator in sets of nine. Just... tapping the keys nine times. It's a Casio, one of the older ones with the really clicky buttons. I love that sound, it's really satisfying. And then sometimes I'll just go stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, just holding them up until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay. Which is usually Susan, our office manager. She's always over there complaining about the toner running out. Toner is so expensive these days, I really don't know how the company affords it with the way she prints every single email out. But yeah, I guess I'm here because I'm doing weird stuff like that.

patient.answer: I'm not really sure... I don't know if it makes me feel less anxious or anything. I haven't really noticed a feeling like that. It's just nine taps. Nine is a really solid number, though. Like, there are nine innings in a baseball game. I used to play baseball back in high school, actually. I played shortstop mostly. Our coach, Mr. Henderson, he used to chew those big wads of Big League Chew bubblegum, the grape flavor. You could smell it from like all the way across the field. He drove this really loud, beat-up Ford pickup truck that he was always trying to fix himself, but it always sounded like the muffler was dragging on the ground. I think he spent more money on parts for that thing than it was even worth. But yeah, I don't really feel any different after I do the tapping or the receipts. I just kind of do it.

doctor.intent: determine if patient's actions are in response to hallucinations or delusions
doctor.question: Do you ever hear voices or see things that others can't?
